steps.text: *pant* *pant* Gotta hurry!
Caulerpa archaeosphaeridium? Here? Who else in Milliarium is cultivating endangered seaweed?

spans.text: ? Here? Who else in Milliarium is cultivating endangered seaweed?

steps.text: Hypnea fenestralis, Halymenia fimbriatus, Palmaria purpureus...
Wait, the color of this Sargassum pennata... I cultivated it myself...
Why are you on the streets... it's too dry. You'll die.
What happened here? Did someone do this?
Where are you migrating? Is there something—
W-Wait!
They're gone?
This pipe...
Wah!
This is...
*cough* Argh—
(What's going on?)
(The rumbling... Is the city moving?)
(Something's moving—who's there?)

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: (Vacuole inflates merrily)

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: I hope I'm not interrupting anything.

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: Not at all. Lucilla and I were just performing regular inspections and maintenance on the city's unit framework.

steps.name: Lucilla
steps.text: Still no sign of Tullia?

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: C'mon, Lucilla, it hasn't been that long since we made the report.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: I can tell you care about her. Did she mention getting into any trouble recently?

steps.name: Lucilla
steps.text: She isn't one to look for trouble. I can't imagine her offending anyone.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: What you say certainly fits her profile. Did she ever talk to you about the Waterway Program or beacon data?

steps.name: Lucilla
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Lucilla
steps.text: I wouldn't say we're close, exactly. We talk from time to time, but she's more of a loner who prefers to work on her own stuff.

steps.name: Lucilla
steps.text: Wait, is she a suspect?

steps.name: Lucilla
steps.text: Sorry, maybe I'm making her sound suspicious...

steps.name: Lucilla
steps.text: B-But it's probably just stress. There's been fighting almost every day in the six months that Milliarium has been away from the home territories. Everyone here is on edge.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: The Church of the Deep continues its attempts to sabotage the Waterway Program. We've eliminated many cultists over those months.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: And until they were exposed, they appeared just like any of our countrymen.

steps.name: Lucilla
steps.text: But she'd have no reason to—

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: Well, to be honest, I've never quite understood why she chose to join the Waterway Program.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: What do you mean, ma'am?

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: You already know that she used to work at the Institute of Ecological Art, right?

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: The IEA moved to another city when this one evacuated its original position and received new battle orders.

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: Right, and she had the chance to go with them to continue her work. But instead, she chose to—

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Sorry to interrupt, but could you explain more about this evacuation you mentioned?

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: You remember, don't you Lucilla? You were working on the dome at the time, so you had the best view of the whole thing.

steps.name: Lucilla
steps.text: ...Yeah.

steps.name: Lucilla
steps.text: It was one of Ægir's largest volcanic power stations, feeding countless laboratories, and Milliarium was responsible for its construction and defense.

steps.name: Lucilla
steps.text: The city was parked beneath the power station. Through the dome, I could see its red glow illuminate the ocean for miles.

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: The heat it generated attracted many different creatures. It was the largest endangered plants reserve in Ægir.

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: And the ideal environment for Milliarium's ecological art to flourish.

steps.name: Lucilla
steps.text: Then, that light turned dark...

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Seaborn?

steps.name: Lucilla
steps.text: Yeah.

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: A year ago, swarms of Seaborn arrived on the ocean currents, and Milliarium ordered an emergency evacuation.

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: Without the natural environment to support it, the Institute of Ecological Art, like other related institutions, was forced to relocate.

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: But there was a full Legion in the city. We could have retaken the power station.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: War orders for the Waterway Program had just arrived. Milliarium was in fact being strategically redeployed.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: I came here with the Legion after that.

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: The lives of so many of our people were changed... including Lucilla.

steps.name: Lucilla
steps.text: By the way, I transferred from the dome to ground work because I was afraid of heights... Sorry, off-topic.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: So you mean to say that Tullia might have had ulterior motives for joining the Waterway Program?

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: That is a serious accusation.

steps.name: Lucilla
steps.text: I don't believe it either.

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: No, no, I'm just telling you what I know.

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: But... it's undeniable that there are a hundred thousand souls in this city, and not all of them are fully committed to the Waterway Program.

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: Most just carry on with their lives, not understanding the kind of path we're clearing out in the ocean.

steps.name: Cassia
steps.text: Even our Iberian guest here came to learn more about the Program, didn't she?

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Whether Tullia is linked with the Church of the Deep or not, the fact remains that she made an unauthorized copy of data on the Waterway Program.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: We'll have to find her to learn why.

steps.name: Lucilla
steps.text: But Milliarium isn't that big. She'd have been found by now, even if she were hiding between dome layers or in the corners of the circulation system.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: True. She may well have already left the city, but we were unable to find her bio-signature in the nearby waters.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Nor were there any unscheduled ship movements at the port. And she couldn't have gone beyond our sensor range in just a few days using civilian deep-water equipment.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: However... the city did make a short movement around 30 hours ago to receive the Iberian mission. Perhaps...

spans.text: make a short movement around 30 hours ago to receive the Iberian mission. Perhaps...

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Could she have left the city at that time?

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: ...So, the Columbian scientist Kristen Wright broke through the barrier for the first time in more than ten thousand years.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: The hole she pierced hasn't completely closed, even after a year. Ægir's surveillance of the universe through this opening continues, and so far no anomalies have been detected.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I tried to stop her, to no avail.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We still have time, but it's running short.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Ripping apart the electron clouds with a high-energy beam... We were not aware of any energy sources on land that could support such a brute-force measure.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Her method came from the same place as Ægir's technology: prehistoric civilization.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: She had discovered sarcophagi beneath Trimounts that preserved that civilization's spark, and managed to obtain the trust of its custodian.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Before leaving the home territories, I had not expected to find anyone with your profound understanding of both Ægir and prehistory from the lands.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: You have demonstrated, once again, that there is still much about Terra we do not understand.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Fins trapped in the depths lose their perception of light. Likewise, our nation must continue to explore, even if we can no longer support grand expansions.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: The stargate, the twin moons, the barrier, the ruins in the mantle... There is much on this planet that was not formed naturally.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Our voyager fleets, having traversed to the far side of the planet, have even detected highly unusual terrain concealed behind the distant dark fog.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: There, the sea currents abruptly cut off, as though they had reached the end of the ocean.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: That is merely a hotbed that has long since cooled. The most important prehistoric relics lie in the Ægir heartlands. You know this, Madame Consul.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The prehistoric ruins beneath the seabed are a gift from the ocean to Ægir. They nurtured your civilization, and have granted you power and knowledge far beyond the terrestrial nations.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: And with them, responsibility.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: As you say, Dr. Kal'tsit, responsibility.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: When did the land dwellers first start calling themselves 'human'? When they lit the first fire with Originium? Built their first city with stone and mud?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: On land, self-awareness and identity were established naturally over time. Even today, humanity is often defined in the narrowest terms.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: For the Ægir, it was conferred. We were not the same race as the Predecessors, but we inherited their identity as we inherited their mantle.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Thus, Ægir was born with a responsibility to humanity. The Seaborn will not compel us to abandon this duty; on the contrary, they add to its weight.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You are indeed the right consul for Milliarium, Madame Consul.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Where is this coming from...?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Your temperament. As Ægir, you are patient and kind.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But that does not diminish the arrogance in your thinking; that is to say, Ægir's arrogance.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I do not believe our conversations about the hole in the barrier, the ruins in the mantle, and even the future of civilization itself, are merely small talk to lighten the mood.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Just as I do not believe Ægir will rely on passive solutions. After all, isn't Millarium's departure from its home territories a proactive effort to create a new line of defense?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: So, my question is, Madame Consul: what is Ægir's endgame for the Waterway?

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: ...I have already told Gladiia Ægir's answer, that which you would call arrogant. You have the right to know as well.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: There is much on this planet that was not formed naturally... and Ægir does not believe they are unrelated.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: Be they wonders like the stargate and the twin moons, or calamities like Originium and the Seaborn, these phenomena cannot be random products of spontaneity. They must be interconnected in some way.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: To solve the Seaborn problem at its source and stop Terra's crisis, we need to fully understand Terra, including the hidden secrets of the land.

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: But those are for the future. If you simply seek my answer for what's at hand...

steps.name: Clementia
steps.text: My endgame for the Waterway is to ensure that hundreds of thousands of Millarium's inhabitants and tens of thousands of Penal Battalion troops in Gran Faro live to see Ægir's main force arrive.

steps.name: 'Little Handy'
steps.text: Distress signal.

steps.name: 'Little Handy'
steps.text: From the squadron tasked with beacon deployment at Nest 37.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: You're sharp.

options: Saved me the effort of looking for you.
Do you always come and go without warning?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: How much has Milliarium told you of the Waterway Program?

options: Thought you'd care more about the Hunters.
Thought you'd care more about your circumstances.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: The tribunal has demonstrated their innocence, and they are not alone.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Besides, Gladiia’s return to Ægir and its conspiracies are of her own accord.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Neither of us is being followed or under surveillance, so my movements have not been exposed.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Let's continue where we left off at the Sophontheatrum.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: The war between Ægir and the Seaborn has gone on for more than two centuries, but both sides have set their sights on dry land at almost simultaneously.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: The sudden migration of an entire species, and a change in direction for an entire nation. Perhaps, deep down, they stem from the same cause.

options: Sounds like you don't trust any of Ægir's plans.
You still have your reservations about us, Ulpianus.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I know more than I've told Gladiia. This extra knowledge forces me to be cautious about Ægir's past and future actions.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: But it's too soon for her to know, and not your place to know at all.

spans.text: But it's too soon for her to know, and not

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Our only concern for now is the Waterway Program.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: A path connecting the land and the sea... Neither that doctor nor the Inquisition fully trust in this, or else you would not be here.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Clearing the seas with powerful weapons to buy time for the main force from the home territories to arrive. Ægir's warfare design is always simple and effective.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: But there have been anomalies in the city that we cannot ignore.

options: I heard about a missing person.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: That consul is a formidable woman.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: During Milliarium's voyage, she has culled many of the corrupted and thwarted their sabotages, while the two escorting Legions have sustained far fewer losses than expected.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Everything has gone well... Almost too well.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Now, a staff member in the Program has gone missing at the most crucial stage. This is just the beginning.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I'm looking into it, and will eliminate any potential threats.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I can enter most places and evade the Sea Patrol's regular rounds with ease.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: But I fear the problem runs deeper.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I would rather not barge into an important lab or the consul's Pensivarium, unless I have to.

options: I'm not your messenger to the Hunters, Ulpianus.
You should work with Rhodes Island, Ulpianus.
After all, we can help you move around the city.
After all, Ægir sees you as a threat, don't they?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Rhodes Island wants to work with me... and watch me, I assume? So be it.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: One more thing.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: ...Skadi.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: If you truly care about the Hunters, keep a close eye on her.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: One hundred fifty-six, one hundred fifty-seven...

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I've never seen a port this busy.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Are things not going well on the frontlines?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: (Humming♪)

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: You're still in the mood for music?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Why not?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Soon we might be too busy for it.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: There you are, Captain Gladiia.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: You went to see Consul Clementia with Dr. Kal'tsit right after the tribunal, right? How did it go?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Well enough, but I was only there to make introductions. They had much to discuss, and I had no reason to stay.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I did have a brief discussion with Clementia on the current plans for the Abyssal Hunters, though.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Ægir's Waterway will open soon. Until then, the Hunters will fight alongside the two Legions accompanying Milliarium.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: See? I was right.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Uh-huh.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: I'd rather be out there killing monsters than sit through another debate.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: So what's the mission and when do we move out?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: The command structure and battle plans are pending discussion with the legion commanders.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Skadi—

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Hey, that's the emergency alarm, right?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: What happened? A Seaborn invasion?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I am Consul Gladiia. Status report.

steps.name: Legion Soldier
steps.text: Yes, ma'am.

steps.name: Legion Soldier
steps.text: Two squadrons from Legion X were sent to deploy the beacon at Nest 37 today, as planned.

steps.name: Legion Soldier
steps.text: But we just received a distress signal. They were attacked by Seaborn on the way.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: The Seaborn were prepared?

steps.name: Legion Soldier
steps.text: Unclear. The situation is still developing. The Academy of Technology hasn't had time to produce a report.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Are there any corvettes on standby in the port?

steps.name: Legion Soldier
steps.text: Always. You can claim one by logging into the terminal.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Thank you. Keep me posted about the squadron's coordinates. Once close enough, the Abyssal Hunters will disembark and swim into battle.

steps.name: Legion Soldier
steps.text: Roger.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Laurentina, with me.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: ...Skadi, you stay behind.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Captain?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Don't overthink it.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: The contact between land and sea is paramount. Kal'tsit can't be in two places at once, so I need you to keep the Doctor safe.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: This is an order.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Received.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: That's...

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Laurentina's group is embarking for battle? But they just came back.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: It has something to do with the alarm. The fleet deploying the beacon at Nest 37 was attacked by Seaborn, and they're going out to help.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: You know the Abyssal Hunters?

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: I do.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: We had a brief partnership on land, facing challenges and battling enemies together, including the Seaborn.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: That's... impressive, given their temperament and fighting style.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: I'd go up and greet Consul Gladiia myself if we weren't in the middle of an emergency. I haven't had the opportunity since they returned.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Does everyone in Ægir know the Hunters?

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Of course not. But I once worked with them... and even aspired to join them.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Someone from your team said you used to be a researcher.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: My expertise in genetic engineering qualified me for the Abyssal Hunter program. I studied under the head of the project, who was also the first Abyssal Hunter.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: At the time, few were compatible, and even fewer successfully underwent the operation. But he and Gladiia had already achieved spectacular results.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Their most remarkable feat was a three-day battle with the Seaborn in a hydrothermal vent that bought time for two energy survey cities to evacuate.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: The Seaborn evolve constantly. With the use of weapons strictly regulated, they were the safest and most effective countermeasure.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: I watched them leave and return every day.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: I watched them lie down in the regenerative gel, exhausted, waiting as I recorded the data, tested their functions, and repaired their bodies. Those were the costs of victory people could not see.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: I'm not entirely sure what motivated me at the time, but one day I submitted an application to become a Hunter to the Institute of Development  Planning.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: ...I'd have done the same.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: I mean, I'd have wanted to apply myself.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: To see your mentor and everyone else risking their lives like that... Nobody would want to feel that they weren't doing enough.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: You seem fit enough, and as a researcher, you are beyond familiar with their functions and combat style. Wait... then why didn't you—

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Because my application was rejected.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: But why?

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: I didn't ask. And my mentor wouldn't have answered.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: So you joined the Sea Patrol instead?

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Because it's the unit that works most closely with the Hunters?

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Yes... and monitors them.

steps.name: Sea Patroller
steps.text: The corvette is ready for you.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Alright.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Sorry, Irene. I shouldn't have bored you with my past.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: It's fine.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Back to work. As the fleet battles the Seaborn, we must also locate the missing scientist for answers. The Sea Patrol's objective remains unchanged.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: As for you, Irene. You're staying with us.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Wait, what for?

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: We won't be in the thick of battle, but it's still dangerous. It's the Sea Patrol's duty to keep you safe.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: I appreciate it, Praefecta. But I'm good.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: I'm not afraid of the Seaborn. Every Inquisitor has Seaborn blood on their hands.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Former Inquisitor, as I recall from your files.

spans.text: Inquisitor, as I recall from your files.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: I appreciate your assistance during the investigation. Like I said, you're sharp... and brave.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: But you didn't come to Ægir to fight. Go back and stay with the other emissaries.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Are you implying that the war between Ægir and the Seaborn is beyond a land dweller's comprehension?

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: ...Yes.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Your concerns are justified, but trying to comprehend is why I'm here.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: There are many things I... as an Iberian, need to understand: Ægir, the Seaborn, true war, and everything that's happening in the depths of the ocean.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: The land isn't far from here. Ægir has only a single city in this region, but beyond it lies the entirety of Iberia.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: Don't worry, I don't intend to get myself killed at sea.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Such maturity at your age... You must have a good mentor.

steps.name: Irene
steps.text: From what I've heard, better than yours, at least.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: ...Prepare a set of deep-water equipment for Irene.

steps.name: Secunda
steps.text: Let's go.
